The HTML file is not a document that opens an app — it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up — about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder — iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive — is ideal.
  2. Double-click MonthlyBudgetPlanner.html. It opens in your browser like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. Four short slides: planning, logging, backups, and your first transaction.
  4. Build your plan once in Monthly budget, then save it as your repeating plan.
  5. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore sample data in the sidebar. A fictional year fills every screen, in a separate session. Return to my budget brings back your own figures, untouched.

The idea

One number, not a balance.

Monthly Plan answers one question first: how much is genuinely free this month?

The Monthly dashboard. After your commitments is what remains once unpaid bills, debt payments and planned contributions are set aside.

Why it is not just your bank balance

A bank balance still counts money already promised to your rent, your card and your savings. This number does not. That is the whole difference — and why it is usually lower than you expect at first.

Green and red mean one thing

Within plan, or over it. Those two colours are reserved for that everywhere in the planner, so you never have to decode them. Hover any chart for the exact figure.

Logging what you spend

Press N anywhere, or choose Add transaction at the top. Quick log takes a short line like coffee 4.50 and files it by matching words — and remembers your choice next time.

Set it once

Plan once. It repeats.

Rebuilding a budget every month is what makes most people stop. This one is built so you do not.

Your repeating plan

Save your budget as the baseline and every new month opens already filled in. Change one figure in March and only March changes — the planner marks it as an override for that month.

Groups that fold away

Income, bills, subscriptions, debt, variable spending and savings each collapse with their own totals, so you can work on one part at a time. Add a category from right here.

Recurring payments

Add rent, the phone, the gym once, on their real rhythm. They appear on the calendar and tick off when you record the matching payment.

Bring it in

Import your bank CSV.

Transactions → Import CSV. Map the columns, review, then add.

It handlesHow
Any date formatDay/month or month/day is decided from the whole column, not guessed row by row.
Your categoriesEvery choice you make is remembered, so the next statement arrives mostly sorted.
DuplicatesRows you already have are flagged and blocked. The same file twice cannot double your spending.
Many rows at onceSelect all, set one category for them all. Closed months reopen from the import itself.

Credit cards: pick one method

Import the card's purchases, or record the payment you make to the card — not both, or the same money counts twice.

Worth finding

Saving up. Paying off.

Savings goals and debt payoff goals, side by side, counted from what you actually log.

Debt payoff

Link a debt category and the goal becomes a payoff: paid off, per cent cleared, and what is still owing.

Cards or table

Search, filter, sort

Keeping your plan safe.

Your plan lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy — including us.

Your entries live in browser storage — please read

  • Everything you enter is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers — a plan built in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your plan.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup — every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every month, goal and category. Restore backup brings it back on any computer.

Daily folder backup — Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this, and Settings says so plainly.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appRight-click the file → Open with → your browser. Extract the ZIP first.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
An import doubled somethingRows marked Possible duplicate can be deleted; future imports block them.
A payoff goal stays at 0%Log the payments made to that debt, not the card's purchases.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
A category is wrongEdit the transaction; create a new category from inside the editor.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Planner currency, or type your own symbol.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Welcome tour → Show tour.
